pairs.why: A keeps a flat slab body with straight edges and tight corners like the real calculator, while B swells into a soft, bulbous rounded blob with a fat bottom.
B draws chunky bollards and thick planked deck up close like the real card, while A shrinks them to thin posts on a distant dock.
B's brim is flatter and crisper and its cone is a clean taper, while A's brim is slightly puffier, but the two shapes are nearly the same.
B has more of the expected parts (door, steps, side tube, antenna) and a taller, solid-walled dome with a base ring, while A is a low squat dome with spindly legs and a ladder.
A has a thick ring-like loop and a rounded, lumpy body similar to the real card's chunky form, but its grooves are deeper than the real ones, so the pair is close.
A has the slimmer, more stacked-tier proportions of the real topiary, while B bulges wider at the base and its tiers are pointier.
A's body is the chubbier, rounder form of the real duck and keeps the mouth closed, whereas B's open mouth and flatter body drift away from it.
A has a thicker top slab and heavier, chunkier pedestal and stools like the real stone table, while B's top is thinner and its stools are slender, lathe-turned shapes.
